# Vendored IM packages

This directory holds the five IM packages derived from [satorijs/satori](https://github.com/satorijs/satori). They keep Satori's platform protocols, wire formats and public names, but their sources are a DSH rewrite rather than a vendored copy, so the log below records how each package currently differs from the Satori pin. The Cordis framework packages and the IM packages' non-IM dependencies (`vendor/element/`, `vendor/http/`, `vendor/fetch-file/`) live in the `vendor/` root and are documented in [vendor/README.md](../README.md), which also owns the generic Build entries (B1–B7) that apply here too; the `@deepseek-ai` npm scope rule is the same as there.

| `core/` | `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-im-core` | `@satorijs/core` | 5.0.0-alpha.0 | https://github.com/satorijs/satori (`packages/core`) | `662c3daff128b4b610ebbc393bac388679e60010` |

The upstream line these packages follow is Satori PR #416 (`feat/v5`, "migrate to cordis v4"), still open at the pin. Their third-party dependencies stay on npm: `path-to-regexp` and `path-to-regexp-typed` (`core/`), the markdown parser closure of `markdown/` (`mdast-util-from-markdown`, `mdast-util-gfm`, `micromark-extension-gfm`, `mdast-util-to-hast`, `hast-util-raw`), and `protobufjs`, `mdast-util-to-markdown` and `mdast-util-gfm` (`adapter-lark/`).

## Local modifications

Keep this log exhaustive: every divergence from the Satori pin must be covered by an entry. Each entry has a stable ID; remove an entry when its divergence no longer exists, never renumber or reuse IDs, and give a new entry the next free `I` number (the next is I15). An entry describes the current divergence, its rationale and the constraints a sync must keep, not the history of how it arose. Every change under `vendor/im/**/src` must update this file in the same commit (enforced by `scripts/check-vendor-manifest.sh`).

- **I1 · Package set and provenance**: five packages come from the Satori pin — `element/`, `core/`, `adapter-lark/`, `adapter-qq/` and `markdown/` — with independently pinned `element`, `http` and `fetch-file` dependencies in the `vendor/` root. Their upstream sources are replaced wholesale (I3–I5, I11, I12) and no upstream IM source is copied verbatim: the platform routes, wire envelopes, protobuf/JSON gateway formats and token endpoints carry over, the rendering pipeline does not. Following PR #416, the protocol module is part of `core/` (`src/protocol.ts`), not a package of its own. Runtime service names, events and `satori:` URLs keep their upstream names. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I2 · Build, metadata and retained API types**: the generic rules of the root log apply — B1 (`package.json`), B2 (`tsconfig.json`), B3 (explicit `.ts` specifiers), B4 (tsdown overrides), B5 (Node-compatible TS) and B7 (`@deepseek-ai` rescope); see [vendor/README.md](../README.md). IM specifics: `core/tsdown.config.ts` is ours and builds two entries, the runtime `lib/index.js` and the `lib/testing.js` testkit behind the `./testing` subpath. The manifests reference each other with `workspace:~`; `markdown/` declares the markdown parser closure (with `hast-util-raw` pinned `~9.1.1`, because 9.2.0 declares `parse5@^8` and calls the tokenizer's removed `flushCharacters`). Every tsconfig compiles under the strict root settings without upstream's nullability, catch and function-variance relaxations. Adapters send multipart bodies through the `undici` `FormData` class (the `http` side is P14 in the root log). `adapter-lark/src/types/` retains only the `auth.ts`, `im.ts` and `contact.ts` API families from `adapters/lark/src/types/` plus the transitive closure of shared declarations in `index.ts` that they and the handwritten sources reference; `src` is published, so the subset ships. Core ecosystem metadata uses `im` and `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-im-*`; README examples use the scoped imports; package READMEs exist only where upstream supplies one, and root Satori documentation is not duplicated. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I3 · `element/` is a typed element vocabulary**: upstream factories and aliases, the global `JSX` declaration and the blanket re-export of `cordis-element` are replaced by a typed `ElementMap` / `VariantMap` / `Element<K>` overlay over the unchanged runtime (`vocabulary.ts`), the block/inline category and tier table (`elements.ts`), the typed `h` factory with an automatic JSX runtime (`factory.ts`), `normalize()` (root `<message>`, flow-container wrapping, envelope and content-model validation; `normalize.ts`), `variantsOf()` / `variantKey()` (`variants.ts`) and the plain projection `toText()` (`text.ts`). Plain strings are literal text; this package parses no markdown (`normalize` keeps `<markdown content>` as one element, joining text children into `content`, and `toText` projects its source; see I4). Vocabulary additions over upstream: `<fallback>`, whose direct children are ranked candidates (a JSX fragment counts as one) normalized into internal `case` children as content of the element the fallback stands in (I5); the "send this text as the user" button variant is `button[type=input]` throughout (`ElementMap.button`, `VariantMap`, core fallback, QQ keyboard `action.type 2`); every `button` takes the optional `ButtonStyle` attributes `size`, `width` (`default | fill | <px>`), `icon`, `confirm` (`{ title, text }`), `tip`, `disabledTip` and `variant` (the exact Lark button types), and `button-group` takes `width` (`auto | fill`) and `align`, with `normalize` rejecting values outside those sets, a non-positive width, an empty icon or tip and an incomplete `confirm`; a blank button label renders an ideographic space, never its action id. Form controls `<form>`, `<input>`, `<select>`, `<option>` are T1 tags (category `control`; content models `flow`, `empty`, `options`, `phrasing`; required `form.name` and `option.value`) with variants `input.checkbox`, `select.multiple` and `button.submit`; a `select` or `input` names its channel with `name` (form key), `id` (own callback) or both, `normalize` validates each control's mode, bounds and value type, keeps `select` children to `option` and rejects `onChange` except on `type="checkbox"`, and `toText` projects a form as the labels and options a reader would have used (`[Title]`, `☑ I agree`, `[选择: A / B]`). Interaction events: `ButtonEvent` gains `respond(answer: ButtonAnswer)` (`{ toast?: { type, content } }`), `defer()` and optional `values` (the submitted form's controls keyed by `name`); `SelectEvent` and `CheckEvent` carry id, values / checked, data, referrer, time and `respond` / `defer`. In `core/`, the fallback table lowers `form` to its children, `input` / `select` to their text reporting `interaction-dropped`, `button.submit` to `button[type=action]`, keeps the `ButtonStyle` attributes when lowering `button.theme`, and renders `button[type=input]` as the label plus its text; `CallbackRegistry` routes `onSelect` through `registerSelect` / `dispatchSelect` and the `interaction/select` event (separate keyspaces, so one id may carry several kinds; a select without `id` registers nothing), `TransformResult.actions` is a `kind`-tagged `InteractionAction` union, and `select` joins the engine's structural-container rule. Covered by `vendor/im/element/tests/{normalize,text,variants}.spec.ts` and `vendor/im/core/tests/{registry,fallback,session,bot,stream,testing}.spec.ts`. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I4 · `markdown/` is a contributed `<markdown>` element**: the upstream `src/markdown.ts` of `packages/element` is split into its own package. It is an ordinary Cordis plugin, not a service: `apply` registers a handler for the `markdown` tag on `Satori.elements` (`ElementContributions`, installed through `ctx.effect`, so unloading withdraws it) and exports `markdown(content)`. `core/` names no markdown: the render engine looks handlers up in the mode registry first and in the contributions second (`RenderBase.contributions`, `HandlerLookup`), so a mode that registers the tag keeps its own handler, and without the plugin the core fallback publishes the source as literal text; `RenderContext.transform(content)` renders content in place of the current element without a degradation entry, and `RenderContext.stream` (`{ strategy, final }`, `StreamPhase`) tells a handler which stream state it renders. Constraint: in an intermediate `append` state the plugin renders only `settledMarkdown` (the source before the last top-level block) of the `<markdown>` that ends the message, because an `append` stream keeps every character it sent while a growing document re-parses (`**ab` → `**abc**`, open fences, setext headings, tables); final states and `patch` / `edit` streams render the whole source. `convert.ts` runs mdast → hast (`mdast-util-to-hast`, raw HTML kept) → `hast-util-raw` → Satori elements, driven by the vocabulary (`resolveTag` via `tagAliases` / `isTag`, `elementInfo` for content models and required attributes), so markdown, HTML tags and every registered element take one path. Only the content categories (inline, block, media) are authorable: controls, renderer directives (`fallback`, `case`) and inbound wrappers (`raw`, `forward`) keep their children as text, so markdown cannot hand a reader a control the sender never sent. Before the HTML stage a self-closing tag with no children (`<at id=ou_x />`) is closed explicitly and GFM footnotes become literal `[^label]` plus their blocks. A block element on its own line becomes that block (`soleBlock`), inside a sentence it keeps its text, and a list item outside its list degrades the same way. `pushText` keeps a newline at either end of a text run as `<br>` unless `trimLineEdges` finds a neighbour that already ends the line; `resolveTag` accepts only own aliases (`Object.hasOwn(tagAliases, name)`, so `<constructor>` stays text); `attrsOf` reads an `at` of type `user` with id `all` or `here` as that mention type. A markdown block's stable id includes the `<markdown>` element's path (`message/markdown[0]>/…`), which feeds Lark card `element_id`s. The Lark adapter imports `fromMarkdown` from this package for inbound `md` nodes, and `dsh-im-bundle` mounts it as `im-markdown`. Covered by `vendor/im/markdown/tests/{convert,element}.spec.ts`, `vendor/im/adapter-qq/tests/stream.spec.ts` and the corpus goldens. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I5 · `core/` render engine and mode selection**: upstream `message.ts` (`MessageEncoder`), the `Methods` / `features` / `supports(name)` surface, the component service and the protocol dependency are gone. Module map: `protocol.ts` public types (`Login`, `User`, `Status`, `Meta`, `WebSocket`, `ChatRef`, `Target`, `UserRef`, `MessageRef`, `InboundMessage`, the `ButtonEvent` augmentation); `mode.ts` `defineMode` and the `LimitKey` table; `registry.ts`, `fallback.ts`, `transform.ts` the transform engine and core fallback table; `degradation.ts` the priced mode score; `directives.ts` the content directives; `resource.ts` (I9); `stream.ts` (I6); `errors.ts` the `PlatformError` taxonomy (I7); `testing.ts` with `testing/` the offline testkit (`FakeAdapter`, shared corpus, conformance, goldens); `bot.ts` the public `Bot` split from the implementer `Adapter`, with one pipeline (`normalize` → `transform` → `prepare` → `serialize` → `sendPayload`), per-publication mode resolution, retries, `PartialSendError` and `edit` / `delete` / `stream` over one handle; `session.ts` the slim `Session` with its `onClick` callback registry; `internal.ts` the `satori:` routes plus `/_api/:name` and `/_tmp/:id`. There is no capability layer (no `capabilities.ts`, `ChatFacts`, `Bot.supports` / `support` / `capabilities`, `Adapter.facts`, `Mode.operations`, `HandlerOptions.available`, `PlatformError.facts`, `RenderContext.caps` / `supports`, chat probes): a mode renders what its registry registers, declared variants included, nothing consults per-chat state, a platform refusal is the classified `PlatformError` of the call, and content that must degrade says so with `<fallback>`. A mode owns its element budget in `assemble` / `check`, and `Bot` runs `mode.check()` on every draft of `send`, `edit` and streams, refusing a violation before any request with `PlatformError('limit', …, { published: 'no' })`. No configuration and no caller picks a mode: an adapter declares `Adapter.modeOrder`, `Bot.send` / `Bot.render` transform every candidate once and take the one losing least, declared order breaking ties, and `RenderResult` reports the resolved mode. The root-level `<meta name="prefer-streamable-mode" value="true" />` keeps only modes with a stream driver (implied by `Bot.stream`), `prefer-expressive-mode` keeps the broadest by counting the `element.*` keys a mode renders natively. `degradationScore` prices losses (media, mentions and mid-message structure above inline formatting, a dropped element most, a folded panel nothing, a later `<fallback>` candidate charged, a `RenderReport.moved` element `COST_PLAIN` so content interleaving text and pictures prefers the mode that keeps them inline); a mode can override a price or forbid a loss. `RenderEngine.render` picks the first `<fallback>` candidate whose whole subtree is native, else the last with the usual lowering, recording it in `RenderReport.fallbacks`. `Bot.stream()` opens in `streamMode()`, the broadest streamable mode (directives applied without content), because a streamed message fixes its content type at the first chunk; `preferredModeId()` only stands in for a `MessageRef` this bot did not send. Covered by `vendor/im/core/tests/{bot,fallback,registry}.spec.ts` and the conformance goldens. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I6 · `core/` stream scheduler**: `stream.ts` drives `patch`, `edit` and `append` streams. Constraints: an unrenderable intermediate state, a refused open and a refused tick are dropped (close renders again and reports), each logging once through the host logger inside its own `try` / `catch` so diagnostics never break a stream. An elapsed `budget.until` does not recall: `Scheduler.finish` attempts `close` first (the platform window ends streaming, not the message) and resends only on a refusal. When the platform refuses a recall (QQ refuses every `DELETE` of a streamed message with `40061001`), `Scheduler.resend` and `limitFail` close the stream on the state it already shows and publish the final state as a fresh message instead of throwing `StreamLimitError` and leaving a message "generating" forever. A confirmed recall clears `Scheduler._handle` (documented on `MessageStream.handle`; `StreamLimitError.handle` keeps the recalled handle for diagnostics), `StreamAbortError.recalled` tells `ImSender` a recalled stream (`failed`) from one still in the chat (`partial`), and `MessageStream.abort()` reports whether the recall removed the message. `Scheduler.context` passes `{ ...options, signal }` so `createEditDriver.open` and every `editPayload` (`Adapter.editPayload`, `EditDriverAdapter.editPayload`, `createEditDriver` `tick` / `close`, `Bot.applyEdit`) receive the lifecycle signal; `Scheduler.abort()` bounds its best-effort `driver.close` with `AbortSignal.timeout(STREAM_ABORT_CLOSE_TIMEOUT_MS)`; the caller-signal listener is removed in `close()`, `fail()` and `abort()`. `Scheduler.retry` retries an initial `driver.open` with `published !== 'no'` only when `StreamHost.idempotentSend` (delegating to `Adapter.idempotentSend`) is true, re-checked after the backoff sleep, keeps an earlier `published: 'unknown'` across retries including `StreamLimitError`, and `tick()` never falls back to `host.send()` after an unknown open. `createEditDriver` drops a handle from its `published` cache when `editPayload` fails, so `close()` still writes the earlier payload. Covered by `vendor/im/core/tests/stream.spec.ts`, `vendor/im/adapter-qq/tests/stream.spec.ts` and `packages/experimental/im/tests/send.spec.ts`. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I7 · Publication outcome semantics**: every `PlatformError` carries `published: 'no' | 'unknown' | …`, which `dsh-im` maps to `failed` (safe to resend) or `uncertain`; a sync must never weaken an `unknown` into `no`. `Bot.send` runs normalize → transform → prepare → serialize inside `unpublished()`, so a pipeline failure (a failed fetch or upload) is `published: 'no'`, passing classified refusals, `StrictRenderError` and `PartialSendError` through. `Bot.withRetry` retries `retryable` / `rate-limit` errors only when `published === 'no'` or the adapter reports `Adapter.idempotentSend?(target, ctx)` (Lark: an `options.idempotencyKey`; QQ: an `idempotencyKey` plus a claimable passive ticket via `PassiveManager.canClaim`), re-evaluated through a callback before and after each backoff sleep so an expiring dedupe window stops the retry; once any attempt was `unknown`, the final error stays `unknown` even if a later attempt says `no`. In both adapters a cancelled request is `fatal` (never retried) but `published: 'unknown'` (an `AbortError` cannot tell "never left" from "answered, body cancelled"), honouring a `published` the error carries; every token-acquisition failure — transport errors, HTTP 4xx/429/5xx (keeping `kind`, `retryAfterMs`, `cause`, `body`), empty token answers, rethrown `PlatformError` / `LarkApiError`, and a caller cancellation while `AccessToken.get(signal)` waits on the shared single-flight `refresh()` (raced without aborting the refresh for other callers) — is `published: 'no'`. `responseOf()` matches a structural `ResponseLike` (`typeof status === 'number'` and `headers.get`), because `undici.fetch`'s `Response` is not the global class. Lark's `LarkApi.answer()` reports an HTTP 200 envelope without `data` as `published: 'unknown'`, like `requiredKey()`. Covered by `vendor/im/core/tests/bot.spec.ts`, `vendor/im/adapter-lark/tests/{errors,bot,send}.spec.ts` and `vendor/im/adapter-qq/tests/{errors,token,send}.spec.ts`. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I8 · Protocol surface consumed by `dsh-im`**: this is the entry a sync is most likely to break silently, because `@deepseek-ai/dsh-im` depends on each signature below and upstream either lacks it or declares it differently. `send` is declared `'send'(bot: Bot, result: SendResult)` and emitted as `ctx.emit('send', this, result)` (upstream: `'send'(session: Session)`, `packages/core/src/index.ts:64` at the pin); `dsh-im` reads `result.handle.parts[0]` and `result.handle.target` to store the bot's own message, so restoring upstream breaks own-message storage and every receipt naming a message. `satori/receive` is an awaited intake event behind `Bot.receive()` while `dispatch()` stays synchronous: the Lark receiver ACKs only after intake consumers settle, and a rejection withholds the ACK without discarding durable state. `Bot.handleOf(ref, mode)` rebuilds a one-part `MessageHandle` (mode id validated, no content claimed) so a message published by an earlier process can be edited or deleted after a restart. `SentPart` carries optional `thread` and `referrer` (Lark fills them from `answer.thread_id`, `answer.root_id`, `target.chat.type` and the sent `message_id`) and `aliases` (QQ fills `answer.ext_info?.ref_idx`, keeping `answer.id` as `part.id`); `InboundMessage.aliases` carries QQ's `message_scene.ext.msg_idx` while `payload.id` stays `message.id`, so `ref_msg_idx` quotes resolve. `Bot.members?(chat, cursor?, limit?)` with `MembersPage` reads a chat's members (absent means `unavailable`). `SessionEvent.reaction.message.chat` is optional and `Session` has a `reaction` getter, because Lark reaction events carry no `chat_id`; Lark emits `reaction-added` / `reaction-removed` regardless and maps an `operator_type === 'app'` operator matching `appId` to `bot.selfId`. Checkbox toggles are a third `CallbackRegistry` keyspace (`registerCheck` / `getCheck` / `dispatchCheck`), an `InteractionAction` `'check'` kind and the `interaction/check` event (`SessionEvent.check`, `Session.check`), re-emitted by `dsh-im` as `im/check` beside `im/select`. Covered by `vendor/im/core/tests/{bot,session}.spec.ts`, `vendor/im/adapter-lark/tests/{ws,send,bot,decode}.spec.ts`, `vendor/im/adapter-qq/tests/{decode,send}.spec.ts`, `packages/experimental/im/tests/{intake,outputs,send}.spec.ts` and `plugin/im-card/test/{service,runtime}.test.ts`. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I9 · Resource fetch and cache**: `createResourceFetcher(ctx, policy)` takes an optional `ResourceFetchPolicy`; without one it reads the body in one call as upstream. `maxBytes` refuses with `ResourceTooLargeError` from `content-length` first, then chunk by chunk without buffering past the limit; `redirect` is forwarded to `ctx.http.get` (`dsh-im` passes `'error'` so an admitted address cannot redirect to a refused one); `timeout` bounds the whole fetch, body included, by joining `AbortSignal.timeout` with the caller's signal and racing every read (`ResourceTimeoutError`), since `ctx.http`'s own timer stops at headers. `abortable` observes a pending read with `void pending.catch(() => {})` before rejecting on an already-aborted signal, so no `unhandledRejection` reaches `app-boot`. The `http/fetch` hook passes `init.signal` into the internal `Request`, races `handleInternalRoute` against it (cancelling a late body) and keeps it across internal 3xx; the `satori:` hook answers its own 3xx and ignores `redirect`. Lark's `/messages/:messageId/resources/:fileKey` and `/images/:imageKey` routes return the upstream `Response` unread (`downloadStream`, `getResourceStream`, `getImageStream`) so `maxBytes` sees `content-length` and can cancel. `prepare` uploads once per key within a call but keeps no cross-publication platform key for a `file:` source (`isMutableSource`); `resourceCacheKey` includes `meta.name`, `mime`, `duration`, `width` and `height`. Covered by `vendor/im/core/tests/{resource,bot}.spec.ts`, `vendor/im/adapter-lark/tests/bot.spec.ts` and `packages/experimental/im/tests/media.spec.ts`. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I10 · Connection lifecycle and gateways**: each run owns its cancellation, retry timers, sockets, initialization, heartbeat, token refresh and event-processing promises; stop aborts setup and connections, cancels timers, closes late sockets, clears fragments and awaits tracked work; concurrent starts keep only the latest controller. Initial retry exhaustion marks the bot offline, an established connection keeps supervised reconnects, initialization failure never marks it online, and a token refresh failure (logged without credentials) closes the connection for reauthentication. `set status` reads `this.ctx.get('satori')?.bots`, so teardown of a fiber without the `satori` inject cannot bury the real error. Client-initiated abnormal closes use `3000` (`undici.WebSocket` rejects codes outside `1000` and `3000–4999`). Lark: the long connection validates envelope and application identity, ignores unselected event families, bounds frame bytes, fragment counts, partial messages and outstanding intake through configuration, expires fragments, ignores identical duplicate segments and rejects conflicting ones; `describeIntakeFailure` unwraps the `AggregateError` of a rejected frame into each listener's `name` and `code`; `card.action.trigger` answers are wrapped as `{ code: 200, data: <base64 JSON> }` (upstream answers none; timing in I11). QQ: every frame is validated, dispatches are serialized in arrival order with independent heartbeats, a missing `HEARTBEAT_ACK` means a half-open socket, and the heartbeat sends `{ op, d: seq ?? null }` (upstream sends `s`); the resume `seq` advances only after `bot.receive` succeeds, a rejection aborts the per-connection controller synchronously and closes with `3000` to `RESUME` from the last persisted seq, while decode failures only log; the `close` listener detaches itself in its own handler so 4006/4007 still run `dropSession()`. Both clients answer a platform-declared failure with a typed error carrying the platform code. Covered by `vendor/im/adapter-lark/tests/ws.spec.ts` and `vendor/im/adapter-qq/tests/ws.spec.ts`. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I11 · `adapter-lark/` rewrite**: modules are `config.ts` (Schemastery: `platform` picks host and reported platform, `cardStreaming`, `callbacks`, `allowAtAll`, `callbackAnswerMs`, long-connection limits), `api/client.ts` (typed REST: message create/reply/update/patch/delete/get/list, chat get and members, image/file upload, resource download, reactions), `api/token.ts` (tenant token, 30-minute refresh window, single-flight), `api/events.ts` (schema-2.0 envelopes, `LarkReferrer`), `errors.ts`, `ws.ts` (protobuf long connection), `bot.ts`, `modes/post.ts` and `modes/card.ts` with their escapers, `prepare.ts`, `send.ts` and `decode.ts`. Errors: `230075` stays `limit` so the scheduler resolves a refused edit by recall-and-resend; an unknown code keeps the platform's own message and code (e.g. `230099`). Streaming: both modes use the core `edit` driver; a card is one `interactive` message replaced by `PATCH /im/v1/messages/{id}`, with no CardKit entity path (no `api/cardkit.ts`, `stream.ts`, card diffing or `card-entity` parts; the card mode declares `patch: never`), because CardKit streaming closes after ten minutes, refuses updating callbacks and makes cards unforwardable; the platform caps edits at 5 QPS per message, which `CARD_STREAM_INTERVAL` (200 ms) respects; post keeps its 20-edit limit; `cardStreaming: false` only selects the buffered `final` strategy. Card markdown: text, code spans and fences go through `mdast-util-to-markdown` with `mdast-util-gfm`; `<` and entity-looking `&` in text use `&#60;` / `&#38;`, code spans stay verbatim (the platform decodes no entity there), only a line consisting of `=` is neutralised, and `linkLabel` escapes `& < > [ ] \` `` ` `` `* _ ~` as numeric entities for bare URLs and link labels because a card shows a backslash. Mentions: `mentionMarkdown` (post) and `cardMention` (card) strip characters outside `[\w-]` from `mention.id` and render a `user` mention with id `all` / `here` as literal `@name`, so only the `all` variant (declared unless `allowAtAll: false`) reaches @everyone. Card controls: buttons serialize the `ButtonStyle` fields (`size`, `width`, `icon` as `standard_icon`, `hover_tips`, `disabled_tips`, `confirm`; `variant` beats `theme`; `button-group` `width="fill"` gives weighted columns, `align` → `horizontal_align`); `button[type=input]` stays undeclared (a card button can only call back); the `action` button variant is declared under `callbacks`; `<form>` → `form`, `<input>` → `input` (`input_type`) or `checker`, `<select>` → `select_static` / `multi_select_static` with `options` and initial values, `<button type="submit">` → `form_action_type: 'submit'` with `name: button.id` (empty names rejected by the client with `200530`; an empty `form` name falls back to `component.id`); selects and checkers carry `{ v4: { id, data } }` unless `callbacks: false`, text inputs report only through `form_value`, and a control with neither form nor callback is `dropped`. `cardActionSession` decodes `select_static` / `multi_select_static` to `interaction/select`, `checker` to `interaction/check`, others to `interaction/button`, and `action.form_value` to `ButtonEvent.values`. `answerCardAction` answers each frame once: `{ toast }` when a listener calls `respond` (resolving after the frame is written, since an earlier card update may be reverted), else `{}` when intake settles (unless deferred) or `callbackAnswerMs` (default 1500, max 2500; the platform drops answers after 3 s) elapses. Media and reactions: uploads need a platform key, a media message is sent once with a caller-owned `uuid`; `deleteReaction()` deletes only this app's reaction after reading the list; `prepare.ts` lookup tables use `Object.create(null)`. Decode: card pictures become `img` with `satori:<platform>/<selfId>/images/<image_key>` served by `getImage` (other apps' keys answer `234008`); `getMessage` returns every item so a `merge_forward` decodes into `<forward>` lines (`sender: content`, nested containers as indented `[合并转发 #id]`, capped by `FORWARD_INDENT_LIMIT`), and entry resources are addressed through the container because entry ids answer `234003`. Members come from `GET /im/v1/chats/{chat_id}/members` (`open_id`, page size ≤ 100, id-less members skipped). Threads: `replyPlan` / `sendMessagePayload` resolve an explicit `Target.thread` to a reply anchor (matching `LarkReferrer`, `ctx.previous[0]`, or `om_…` / `omt_…` lookups verifying `chat_id`, read failures `published: 'no'`) and post with `reply_in_thread: true`, because `createMessage` has no `thread_id`; a stored referrer without thread metadata falls through to `resolveReplyMessageId`. Covered by `vendor/im/adapter-lark/tests/{bot,card,post,send,stream,ws,decode,errors,prepare}.spec.ts`, the card/post goldens and `packages/experimental/im/tests/{send,outputs}.spec.ts`. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I12 · `adapter-qq/` port**: modules are `config.ts` (`transport: 'ws' | 'none'`, so a REST-only client opens no gateway; `passive.seqBase` starting at 2 because `msg_seq` is deduplicated per `(msg_id, msg_seq)`; configurable `baseUrl` and `tokenUrl`), `token.ts` (refresh at `expires_in − 60 s`, single-flight, a still-valid token served when refresh fails), `api.ts` (v2 REST: gateway, group/C2C messages, files, recall, interaction acknowledgement, `GET /users/@me`, C2C `stream_messages`; `group:<openid>` / `user:<openid>` addressing), `errors.ts` (code table, `304…` quota family, HTTP fallbacks), `passive.ts` (passive-reply windows, per-event `msg_seq` budget, remaining replies for a stream; `shrink()` never evicts a window with live tickets, so `max` is a soft bound), `modes/text.ts`, `modes/markdown.ts`, `keyboard.ts`, `prepare.ts`, `send.ts` (passive bookkeeping, dedupe retry), `stream.ts` (C2C `append` driver), `ws.ts` and `decode.ts`. `gatewayUrl()` parses both URLs and replaces the host only when it differs, keeping the served host (sandbox included). `GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE` decodes like `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`, but the `<@…>` mention stays in place and `mentions.self` is set only when the body mentions the bot's `union_openid`, read once via `QQBot.ensureIdentity` (`READY` omits it; a failed read leaves the message unaddressed). Markdown mode: `code` is a backtick span and `pre` a fenced block of `verbatim` nodes copied without escaping, collapsing or `\u200B` padding; narrow tables reach the chat as a monospace fenced grid (QQ renders no tables); `flattenRuns` lets list items and quotes prefix every line including fences; inline metacharacters take a backslash while block markers take a leading U+200B because QQ ignores `\#`, `\-` and `1\.`; `img` renders inline as `![alt #Wpx #Hpx](qqbot-media://…)` (`assemble` placeholder filled by `serialize` after `prepare` uploads), while the text mode keeps the `msg_type: 7` media message. Streaming: `stream_messages` sends the whole state as `content_raw` with `input_mode: 'replace'`, takes the stream id from the first answer's `id`, and `assertRoom` treats `remain_msg_len: 0` as unmeasured. Sync caveat: upstream `src/` at the pin is a different file set (`bot/`, `internal/`, `http.ts`, `message.ts`, `types.ts`, `utils.ts`, `ws.ts`), so port upstream changes into these modules; never copy the directory over them. Covered by `vendor/im/adapter-qq/tests/{bot,decode,markdown,stream,passive}.spec.ts` and the mode goldens. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

- **I13 · Core rc.12 compatibility**: `core/src/session.ts` reads `bot.ctx[Context.root]` instead of `bot.ctx.root`. Retire: when `core/` synchronizes against Cordis Core rc.12.

- **I14 · `adapter-qq/` mentions, interaction ids and platform-named failures**: `<at>` is registered in the `markdown` mode only — the `user` variant writes `<qqbot-at-user id="…" />` (the id stripped to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, an id the tag cannot carry renders nothing) and the `all` variant writes `<qqbot-at-everyone />`, because QQ reads those tags only inside a markdown body; `here` and `role` stay undeclared and take the core's readable fallback, so the text mode keeps `@name` and a message carrying a mention resolves to markdown. A click's `event_id` goes out as `INTERACTION_CREATE:<id>` (`eventIdOf`, prefix passed through when the id already carries it), because the gateway reports the interaction as a bare uuid that a message body refuses with `40034025`; a refusal of that field falls back to one active send, which cannot duplicate anything because the refusal published nothing. `QqApi.request` names the platform's own `code` and `message` in the error it raises (`… answered 400 (code 40034105: 主动消息失败, 无权限)`), and `classify` keeps that sentence for a code the table does not list instead of the status rule's anonymous one; `40034105` (permission), `40034128` (invalid) and `40034025` (invalid) joined the table. Covered by `vendor/im/adapter-qq/tests/{api,errors,send,markdown}.spec.ts` and the refreshed markdown goldens. Retire: DSH-owned; permanent unless upstreamed into Satori.

## Sync procedure

The upstream is a moving PR line (#416), and there is no copy-over sync because the sources are rewritten. Diff upstream between the pinned commit and the target commit, port each relevant change into the rewritten modules (for `adapter-qq/` see the I12 caveat), keep the I8 contracts intact, update this log and the manifest commit, then re-run `pnpm run rescope-vendor --apply` per root B7 and run the `vendor/im/*/tests` suites plus the `packages/experimental/im*` tests.
